literature_source: GeneCards MT-CO1; Wikipedia/OMIM Cytochrome c oxidase subunit I

literature_source: GeneCards COX4I1; Oncotarget 2015 (COX4I1 regulates BMI1, glioma proliferative capacity); ASH 2023 abstract (COX4I1 controls AML progression)
note: Complex IV subunit IV (COX4I1); mainly housekeeping OXPHOS subunit, though a few studies link it to glioma/AML proliferation - not enough for a general oncogene call; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: J Mol Endocrinol 2012 "Multiple roles of COUP-TFII in cancer initiation and progression"; Acta Pharmacol Sin 2015 review; Oncol Lett 2025 "The role of NR2F2 in cancer" review
note: NR2F2/COUP-TFII orphan nuclear receptor with well-documented dual, tissue- and stage-dependent roles (pro- and anti-tumorigenic) across cancer types; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: Multiple AACR/Clin Cancer Res reviews on XPO1/selinexor (e.g. "The past, present and future of CRM1/XPO1 inhibitors", Stem Cell Investig); Nat Commun 2026 preclinical XPO1 inhibitor paper
note: XPO1/CRM1 nuclear export receptor is overexpressed and required for tumor cell survival across many cancers, validated drug target (selinexor, FDA-approved); CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Blood 2006 "CXCR4: a key receptor in the crosstalk between tumor cells and their microenvironment"; Biomarker Res 2025 "Targeting the chemokine receptor CXCR4 for cancer therapies"
note: Chemokine receptor consistently shown to promote metastasis, invasion and poor prognosis across solid and hematologic cancers; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Cancer Res 2014 "Loss of Cdk2 and Cyclin A2 Impairs Cell Proliferation and Tumorigenesis"; GeneCards CCNA2
note: Cyclin A2 (CCNA2) drives S/G2-M cell-cycle progression; canonical proliferation oncogene, frequently overexpressed in cancer; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: PNAS 2013 CCNE1 amplification synthetic lethality with BRCA1 loss; PMC "Down-regulation of the cyclin E1 oncogene... induces cell cycle arrest"; MD Anderson Sci Rep 2022 CCNE1 amplification cohort
note: Cyclin E1 (CCNE1) is a canonical, frequently-amplified G1/S oncogene (ovarian, breast, endometrial cancers); CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Oncogene 2017 "Cyclophilin D counteracts p53-mediated growth arrest and promotes Ras tumorigenesis" (pro-tumor); Sci Rep 2025 "Cyclophilin D suppresses colorectal cancer progression through autophagy-mediated apoptosis" (anti-tumor); JBC "Cyclophilin D interacts with Bcl2, anti-apoptotic effect"
note: PPIF/cyclophilin D shows genuinely opposing roles across cancer contexts (pro-tumorigenic in RAS-driven models, tumor-suppressive in colorectal cancer models); CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: GeneCards/NCBI KRT19; used clinically as CYFRA21-1 biomarker fragment
note: Structural intermediate filament/epithelial differentiation marker, not a signaling oncogene or tumor suppressor; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: GeneCards DDB1; Cancer Sci 2009 review "Ubiquitin-mediated control of oncogene and tumor suppressor gene products"; Cell/Mol Cell DCAF-CUL4-DDB1 substrate-receptor literature
note: DDB1 is a shared scaffold for the CUL4-DDB1-DCAF ubiquitin ligase that targets both oncoproteins and tumor suppressors depending on the DCAF substrate receptor recruited; direction is substrate-context dependent; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: Cancer Res 2022 "DNA-PKcs: A Targetable Protumorigenic Protein Kinase" (AACR review); Clin Cancer Res 2019 "Pleiotropic Impact of DNA-PK in Cancer"; Cancer Res 2024 "PRKDC Induces Chemoresistance in Osteosarcoma...Activate AKT"
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. S2056 is the major DNA-PKcs autophosphorylation/activation cluster; current major reviews classify DNA-PKcs as protumorigenic (beyond its DNA-repair caretaker role), promoting therapy resistance and pro-survival AKT signaling - the phospho-signal marks an engaged, protumorigenic-leaning kinase rather than a neutral repair readout.

literature_source: Same reviews as above (Cancer Res 2022 AACR; Clin Cancer Res 2019); PNAS 2020 T2609 cluster and repair-pathway choice; Cancers 2020 "Beyond DNA Repair: DNA-PKcs in Tumor Metastasis, Metabolism and Immunity"
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. T2609 cluster (ATM/ATR-mediated) is an activation-associated phosphorylation of DNA-PKcs; consistent with the field's current protumorigenic classification of activated DNA-PKcs signaling (metastasis, metabolism, immune evasion functions beyond repair).

literature_source: Cancer Res 2022 AACR "DNA-PKcs: A Targetable Protumorigenic Protein Kinase"; Cancers 2020 "Beyond DNA Repair: DNA-PKcs in Tumor Metastasis, Metabolism and Immunity"
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. Y393 is a Src-family-kinase-associated activation mark on DNA-PKcs; scored consistently with the other DNA-PKcs activation phosphosites given the field's current protumorigenic-kinase classification.

literature_source: GeneCards TOP1; ScienceDirect 2025 "Targeting DNA Topoisomerase I for the Treatment of Cancer: Past, Present and Future"
note: Essential replication/transcription enzyme and chemotherapy target (irinotecan/topotecan), not classified as an oncogene or tumor suppressor per se; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: PubMed 2024 "The role of E2F2 in cancer progression and its value as a therapeutic target"; PMC "Expression and Prognostic Role of E2F2 in Hepatocellular Carcinoma"
note: Activating E2F-family transcription factor driving G1/S cell-cycle gene expression; broadly classified as proliferative/oncogenic; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: PubMed 2018 "FABP4 suppresses proliferation and invasion of hepatocellular carcinoma cells, predicts poor prognosis" (tumor-suppressive in HCC); AACR Cancer Res 2020 "Adipocyte-Induced FABP4...Promotes Metastasis and Mediates Carboplatin Resistance" in ovarian cancer (oncogenic)
note: FABP4/E-FABP shows genuinely opposite roles across cancer types (suppressive in HCC, pro-metastatic in ovarian cancer via adipocyte crosstalk); CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: PMC "Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Cell Proliferation Signaling Pathways"; Thermo/CST phospho-EGFR(Y992) product literature (PLCγ1-recruitment site)
note: Y992 is a PLCγ1-binding activation site on ligand-activated EGFR; canonical marker of active oncogenic RTK signaling; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: ScienceDirect review "Roles of the translation initiation factor eIF2α serine 51 phosphorylation in cancer formation and treatment"; Nat Commun 2021 "integrated stress response is tumorigenic...in KRAS-driven lung cancer"; Cell Death Dis "eIF2α-S51 phosphorylation determines Akt-dependent cell-fate decisions in oxidative stress"
note: Inhibitory phosphomark that both suppresses bulk translation and activates the integrated stress response; literature shows this ISR arm can be tumor-adaptive/pro-survival in some contexts and pro-apoptotic in others depending on stress duration/intensity - genuinely dual; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: PubMed 2023 "Eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A1 in the pathogenesis and treatment of cancers"; Cancer Discov "Inhibition of eIF4A RNA Helicase Activity Blocks Oncogene Translation"; PubMed "RNA G-quadruplexes cause eIF4A-dependent oncogene translation in cancer"
note: eIF4A1 selectively drives cap-dependent translation of oncogenic mRNAs (MYC, cyclins) and is a validated anticancer drug target; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Same as eif2aps51 (ScienceDirect eIF2α-S51 review; Nat Commun 2021 ISR tumorigenic in KRAS lung cancer)
note: Alternate/garbled naming of the same eIF2α phospho-Ser51 antibody as eif2aps51; identical dual-role rationale; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: Nat Rev Cancer 2013 "Endothelin 1 in cancer: biological implications and therapeutic opportunities"; Cancer Res 2009 "Endothelin-1 Stimulates Lymphatic Endothelial Cells...to Grow and Invade"; Trends Endocrinol Metab "Emerging role of endothelin-1 in tumor angiogenesis"
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. Contrary to the draft's "context-dependent" call, the literature on EDN1/endothelin-1 in cancer is fairly convergent: it consistently promotes tumor cell proliferation, invasion, angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis across multiple solid tumor types (ovarian, prostate, colorectal, melanoma), supporting a growth-promoting classification.

literature_source: Mol Biol Rep 2026 "EphA2 as an oncogenic driver: roles and mechanisms of action in cancer"; PMC "EphA2 expression is a key driver of migration and invasion and a poor prognostic marker in colorectal cancer"
note: Overexpressed, ligand-independent oncogenic RTK promoting invasion/migration/poor prognosis across many solid tumors; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Mol Biol Cell 2016 "PKA can block EphA2 receptor-mediated cell repulsion by increasing EphA2 S897 phosphorylation"; Oncogene 2021 "Oncogenic functions and therapeutic targeting of EphA2 in cancer"
note: S897 is an Akt/RSK-mediated phosphorylation that suppresses EphA2's canonical ligand-dependent tumor-suppressive (repulsive) signaling and instead drives ligand-independent, pro-migratory/invasive non-canonical signaling; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: PMC1242143 (Bostner et al., "Phosphorylation of ERα serine 167 predictive of response to endocrine therapy and increased postrelapse survival"); PubMed 17908967 and 18550720 (pS167 linked to longer disease-free/overall survival)
note: Mechanistically, S167 is an Akt/S6K1-driven activating phosphorylation that enhances ERα transcriptional (proliferative target-gene) activity, so it is kept at +1 on that mechanistic basis; confidence downgraded from the draft's High to Medium because several clinical cohorts paradoxically link high pS167 to BETTER endocrine-therapy response and longer survival (likely reflecting luminal differentiation/subtype rather than proliferative drive) - flagging this tension for reviewer attention.

literature_source: MedlinePlus ERCC2 gene summary; nucleotide excision repair gene, mutations cause xeroderma pigmentosum/trichothiodystrophy (cancer-predisposition syndromes)
note: XPD/ERCC2 is a genome-caretaker NER gene; loss-of-function predisposes to cancer, consistent with a tumor-suppressive ("caretaker") classification like other DNA-repair genes in this panel; CONFIRMED at -1.

literature_source: Oncogene 2016 "The oncogene ERG: a key factor in prostate cancer"; PubMed 2022 "The Expression of Proto-Oncogene ETS-Related Gene (ERG) Plays a Central Role in...Prostate Cancer"
note: TMPRSS2-ERG fusion is one of the most common and best-characterized oncogenic drivers in prostate cancer; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: ScienceDirect review "Targeted Avenues for Cancer Treatment: The MEK5-ERK5 Signaling Pathway"; note: Cell Cycle 2016 shows KRAS/BRAF-mutant or MAPK7-amplified lines are not uniformly "addicted" to ERK5 activity
note: MAPK7/ERK5 is broadly classified as a proliferative/pro-survival MAPK-family kinase and an active drug-target pathway (MEK5-ERK5), though dependency is not universal across all tumor genotypes; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Blood 2011 "ETV6 Is An Early T-Cell Progenitor (ETP)-Specific Tumor Suppressor Gene in Adult T-ALL"; ScienceDirect "ETV6: A versatile player in leukemogenesis"; ASH "Molecular basis of ETV6-mediated predisposition to childhood ALL"
note: ETS-family transcriptional repressor with well-established tumor-suppressor function in hematopoiesis; its disruption (deletion, point mutation, or fusion such as ETV6-RUNX1) drives leukemogenesis; CONFIRMED at -1.

literature_source: Oncogene "Intrinsic FAK activity and Y925 phosphorylation facilitate an angiogenic switch in tumors"; Mol Biol Cell 2011 "FAK phosphorylation at Tyr-925 regulates cross-talk between focal adhesion turnover and cell protrusion"
note: Y925 is a Grb2-binding activation site on FAK that drives Ras-Erk signaling, focal-adhesion turnover, angiogenesis and invasion; canonical oncogenic activation marker; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: PMC "Fanconi Anemia Signaling and Cancer"; Cancer Biol Ther 2014 "Advances in the understanding of the Fanconi Anemia tumor suppressor pathway"
note: Core component of the Fanconi Anemia/BRCA DNA-repair pathway; well-established tumor-suppressor whose loss causes genomic instability and cancer predisposition; CONFIRMED at -1.

literature_source: Cell Signaling Technology / R&D Systems phospho-FGFR(Y653/Y654) product descriptions (activation-loop autophosphorylation sites); established FGFR oncogenic-driver literature
note: Y653/Y654 are the FGFR kinase activation-loop autophosphorylation sites, the canonical marker of activated FGFR signaling, an established oncogenic RTK pathway across multiple cancers; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Frontiers Mol Biosci 2021 "Upregulation of Translationally Controlled Tumor Protein Is Associated With Cervical Cancer Progression"; ScienceDirect review "The multifaceted potential of TPT1 as biomarker and therapeutic target"
note: TCTP/fortilin (TPT1) is broadly anti-apoptotic and overexpressed/pro-survival across multiple cancer types; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Cell Signaling Technology phospho-FoxO3a(Ser318/321) product notes (Akt substrate site); ScienceDirect "Akt, FoxO and regulation of apoptosis"; PMC "Inhibition of AKT promotes FOXO3a-dependent apoptosis in prostate cancer"
note: CORRECTED from -1 to +1. S318/S321 is the canonical Akt-mediated inactivating phosphorylation that excludes FOXO3a from the nucleus and shuts down its tumor-suppressive transcriptional program (e.g. p27, BIM induction). Although total FOXO3a is tumor-suppressive, THIS phospho-mark specifically reports active oncogenic PI3K/AKT pathway signaling - the RPPA signal represents pathway activation, not tumor-suppressor activity, so it should carry the same sign as other activated-AKT-pathway readouts (analogous to phospho-GSK3 below), not the sign of the unphosphorylated parent.

literature_source: Oncogene 2020 "The nuclear oncoprotein Fra-1: a transcription factor knocking on therapeutic applications' door"; PMC "Role of the Transcription Factor FOSL1 in Organ Development and Tumorigenesis"
note: S265 is an ERK-mediated phosphorylation that stabilizes and activates the Fra-1/FOSL1 oncoprotein, promoting EMT/invasion; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Same as fra1ps265 (Oncogene 2020 Fra-1 review; PMC FOSL1 tumorigenesis review) - cleaved-form-specific variant of the same phospho-antibody
note: Cleaved-form-specific version of the FRA1 pSer265 antibody; same target/rationale as fra1ps265; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Cancer Res 2013 "Amplification of FRS2 and Activation of FGFR/FRS2 Signaling Pathway in High-Grade Liposarcoma"; PMC "Discovery of a small molecule ligand of FRS2 that inhibits invasion and tumor growth"
note: Y436 phosphorylation of the FRS2 adaptor recruits Grb2/PI3K downstream of FGFR and other RTKs, propagating oncogenic Ras/PI3K signaling; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Oncogene 2010 "Focal amplification and oncogene dependency of GAB2 in breast cancer"; Nat Med "A role for the scaffolding adapter GAB2 in breast cancer"
note: GAB2 is a focally amplified, oncogene-dependency scaffold in breast cancer; pY452 marks the activated adaptor recruiting PI3K/p85; confidence upgraded from draft's Medium to High given the strength/consistency of the amplification literature; CONFIRMED at +1.

literature_source: Cancer Cell 2008 "GATA-3 Links Tumor Differentiation and Dissemination in a Luminal Breast Cancer Model"; PMC "GATA3 Inhibits Breast Cancer Metastasis through the Reversal of Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition"; Cell Death Dis 2019 "GATA3 recruits UTX for gene transcriptional activation to suppress metastasis of breast cancer"
note: Majority of functional literature supports an anti-metastatic, luminal-differentiation-promoting (tumor-suppressive) role for GATA3 in breast cancer, despite one review title framing it as debated; CONFIRMED at -1.

literature_source: Front Cell Dev Biol 2020 "Glycogen Phosphorylase B Is Regulated by miR101-3p and Promotes Hepatocellular Carcinoma Tumorigenesis"; PLOS ONE 2019 "Breast cancers utilize hypoxic glycogen stores via PYGB...to promote metastatic phenotypes"; PMC 2025 "Aberrant expression of PYGB as a potential therapeutic target...in lung cancer"
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. "GPBB" = glycogen phosphorylase, brain-type isoenzyme (gene PYGB). Multiple independent studies across HCC, breast and lung cancer converge on PYGB promoting tumorigenesis/metastasis by fueling glycogenolysis-based metabolic reprogramming under hypoxia, more consistent than a purely "housekeeping metabolic enzyme" framing.

literature_source: PubMed 2025 "The duality of GSK-3β in urinary bladder cancer: Tumor suppressor and promoter roles through multiple signaling pathways"; Spandidos review "Glycogen synthase kinase 3β in tumorigenesis and oncotherapy"
note: Total/pan GSK3α/β antibody; GSK3 has well-documented dual, pathway- and cancer-type-dependent roles (Wnt-suppressive arm vs. NF-κB/survival-promoting arm); CONFIRMED at 0 for the non-phospho (total-protein) readout.

literature_source: Same GSK3 dual-role reviews as above, plus mechanistic rationale (Ser21/Ser9 is the Akt-inactivating site; PMC4340754 "Glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK3): regulation, actions, and diseases")
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. Ser21(α)/Ser9(β) phosphorylation is the canonical Akt-mediated INACTIVATING mark on GSK3; loss of GSK3 activity stabilizes β-catenin and cyclin D1, promoting proliferation. As with phospho-FOXO3a, this phosphosite should be scored as a readout of oncogenic PI3K/AKT pathway activation, not by the dual biology of total GSK3.

literature_source: Same rationale/sources as gsk3alphabetaps21 (combined α-Ser21/β-Ser9 dual-inactivating-phosphosite antibody)
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. Combined alpha/beta inactivating phosphosite antibody; same Akt-pathway-activation rationale as gsk3alphabetaps21 and gsk3bps9.

literature_source: Spandidos review "Glycogen synthase kinase 3β in tumorigenesis and oncotherapy (Review)"; ScienceDirect "GSK3B - an overview"
note: Total GSK3-beta protein antibody; dual/context-dependent role in cancer (tumor-suppressive via Wnt/β-catenin degradation vs. pro-tumor via NF-κB and other substrates); CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: Frontiers 2016 "Novel Non-phosphorylated Serine 9/21 GSK3β/α Antibodies: Expanding the Tools for Studying GSK3 Regulation"; PMC4340754 GSK3 regulation review; Karger "AKT/GSK3β Signaling in Glioblastoma"
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. Ser9 is the principal Akt-mediated inactivating phosphosite on GSK3β and a standard RPPA readout of active oncogenic PI3K/AKT signaling (used this way in TCGA/TCPA pathway scoring); scored by pathway-activation logic rather than by GSK3's own dual biology.

literature_source: Same sources as gsk3alphabetaps21/gsk3bps9 (GSK3 Ser21/Ser9 Akt-inactivation literature)
note: CORRECTED from 0 to +1. Ser21-specific (GSK3-alpha) inactivating phosphosite; same Akt-pathway-activation rationale as the other phospho-GSK3 entries.

literature_source: Leukemia 2010 "γH2AX: a sensitive molecular marker of DNA damage and repair"; Cancer Res 2011 "Phosphorylation of H2AX at Ser139...Inhibits Cell Transformation"
note: γH2AX is a downstream readout of DNA damage/replication stress engagement (checkpoint/repair-focus marker), not itself a growth-promoting or growth-inhibiting signaling node; one study even links this phosphorylation to inhibition of cell transformation. Genuinely a "readout, not a driver" case; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: R&D Systems "Human cIAP-1/HIAP-2 Antibody" and "cIAP-2/HIAP-1" product pages (historical aliases); general IAP-family (BIRC2/BIRC3/BIRC5/XIAP) anti-apoptotic cancer literature (e.g. Cancer Cell Int 2016 "Survivin: a unique target for tumor therapy")
note: HIAP is a historical alias for a cellular IAP-family member (cIAP1/BIRC2 or cIAP2/BIRC3 - the antibody name alone does not disambiguate which). All characterized IAP-family proteins are anti-apoptotic and generally pro-survival/oncogenic-supportive (amplified in several cancers, promote NF-κB signaling and chemoresistance), so the directional call (+1) is robust even though the exact paralog identity is uncertain; CONFIRMED at +1, confidence kept at Medium due to name ambiguity.

literature_source: PMC 2024 "Roles of Histone H2A Variants in Cancer Development, Prognosis, and Treatment"
note: Generic/core (non-variant-specific) histone H2A; structural chromatin protein commonly used as an RPPA loading-control-type marker, no oncogene/TSG classification (context-specific roles exist only for named H2A variants such as macroH2A/H2A.Z, not the pan-H2A antibody); CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: Cancer Cell 2023 "Immune checkpoint HLA-E:CD94-NKG2A mediates evasion of circulating tumor cells from NK cell surveillance"
note: HLA-E facilitates tumor immune evasion (an indirect pro-tumor mechanism via NK/T-cell inhibition) but has no established direct role in cell-intrinsic proliferative or growth-suppressive signaling, the axis this fs score is meant to capture; CONFIRMED at 0.

literature_source: Clin Cancer Res 2013 "HMGB1 in Cancer: Good, Bad, or Both?"; PMC 2024 "Multiple functions of HMGB1 in cancer"
note: Extensively documented dual role: pro-tumorigenic via inflammatory/autophagy/pro-survival signaling in some contexts, but also drives antitumor immunity as a DAMP and can promote apoptosis in others; CONFIRMED at 0.
